src: The New York Times · TIME · United Nations

a.title: International Day of Charity
text: September 5 is the International Day of Charity. It is a special day made by the United Nations.
Charity means helping other people — often by giving money, food, time, or kindness.
The day is on September 5 because a famous helper, Mother Teresa, died on this day in 1997. She spent her life helping poor and sick people.
On this day, people think about others who need help. Some give money to good causes. Some give old clothes, food, or their time.
You do not need to be rich to help. A small act of kindness can also make someone's day better.
Helping others feels good. When we help one another, our world becomes a kinder place.

q.q: What is this text mainly about?
opts: A day about helping others, and why it matters
q.why: 全文介紹國際慈善日，以及「幫助別人」為什麼重要。

q.q: Why is the day on September 5?
opts: It is the start of school
It is the day Mother Teresa died in 1997
It is a public holiday in Taiwan
It is the middle of autumn
q.why: 第三段：the day is on September 5 because Mother Teresa died on this day in 1997。

q.q: According to the text, what does charity mean?
q.why: 第二段：Charity means helping other people。

q.q: In the text, a “cause” is ___.
opts: a good aim or idea that people support
q.why: cause = 值得支持的理念、目標。give money to good causes 就是捐給好的公益目標。

q.q: What does the text suggest about helping others?
opts: Even a small act of kindness matters
Helping is a waste of time
You must give money to help
q.why: 第五段：You do not need to be rich…a small act of kindness can also make someone's day better。

b.title: Small Acts, Big Difference
text: Every year on 5 September, the United Nations marks the International Day of Charity, a reminder that helping others is one of the oldest and most powerful of human habits.
The date was not chosen by chance. It is the anniversary of the death of Mother Teresa, the nun who won the Nobel Peace Prize for her work among the poor and the sick in India.

Charity today takes many forms. People donate money to relief groups, volunteer at food banks, give blood, or simply check on a lonely neighbour. Online giving has also made it easier to support causes far away.
Experts say charity does more than help those in need. Studies suggest that people who give — whether time or money — often feel happier and less stressed themselves.
Still, charity has its critics. Some argue that governments, not private giving, should solve big problems like poverty, and that donations can sometimes hide deeper unfairness in society.
Whatever the debate, the message of the day is gentle but firm: no act of kindness is too small, and a caring society is built one good deed at a time.

q.q: Which sentence best states the main idea?
opts: The International Day of Charity celebrates helping others, in many forms and for many reasons.
q.why: 全文圍繞國際慈善日：助人的價值、方式、好處與爭論。

q.q: Why was 5 September chosen for the day?
opts: It is the anniversary of Mother Teresa's death
It is the first day of autumn
q.why: 第二段：It is the anniversary of the death of Mother Teresa。

q.q: Which is NOT given as a form of charity?
q.why: 第三段列出捐款、志工、捐血、關心鄰居等；得諾貝爾獎不是文中所說的行善方式。

q.q: In paragraph 3, “donate” is closest in meaning to ___.
opts: to give, especially to a good cause
q.why: donate = 捐贈，通常是給公益團體。

q.q: What point do the critics in paragraph 5 make?
opts: Big problems like poverty may need governments, not just private giving
q.why: 第五段：批評者認為像貧窮這樣的大問題應由政府解決，私人捐助有時會掩蓋更深的不公。

c.title: The Uses and Limits of Giving
text: Each 5 September the United Nations observes the International Day of Charity, an occasion timed to the death of Mother Teresa and devoted to a deceptively simple idea: that people ought to help one another.

Few would argue with the sentiment. Charity is among the most universal of human impulses, praised by every major tradition and, research suggests, quietly good for the giver as well as the recipient; generosity is repeatedly linked to lower stress and greater life satisfaction.

Yet the day also invites harder questions. Critics of what some call “the charity model” warn that private giving, however well-meant, can treat the symptoms of poverty while leaving its causes untouched — and can even let governments and companies off the hook. A food bank feeds the hungry tonight; it does not ask why they are hungry.

Others worry about visibility: the danger that giving becomes performance, a display of virtue rather than a quiet transfer of help. The most admired traditions of charity, tellingly, prize the gift that is given anonymously.
None of this is an argument against generosity. It is, rather, a reminder that kindness and justice are not the same thing, and that a humane society needs both.
That may be the day's quiet lesson: to give freely, but also to imagine a world in which far less giving would be needed.

q.q: Which best captures the writer's overall point?
opts: Charity is pointless and should stop.
Charity is valuable, but kindness alone cannot replace justice.
q.why: 作者肯定慈善的價值，卻提醒「善意」不等於「公義」，社會兩者都需要（第5段）。

q.q: In paragraph 3, treating “the symptoms of poverty while leaving its causes untouched” means charity may ___.
opts: ease the visible effects without fixing the root problem
q.why: symptom（表徵）對比 cause（根源）：只緩解看得見的困苦，卻未解決造成貧窮的根本原因。

q.q: Why does the writer mention giving that is “given anonymously”?
opts: To say anonymous gifts are illegal
To contrast quiet, genuine help with giving done as a show of virtue
To prove charity does not work
q.why: 第四段擔心行善變成「表演美德」，因此推崇匿名的付出——真正的幫助而非展示。

q.q: How would you describe the writer's attitude to charity?
q.why: 作者支持慷慨（None of this is an argument against generosity），但同時提出反思——是「支持但帶批判」的態度。

q.q: What is the role of “Yet” at the start of paragraph 3?
opts: To turn from praise of charity to harder questions about it
q.why: 第2段肯定慈善，第3段用 Yet 轉折，帶出對「慈善模式」的質疑，形成對比。

discuss: Have you ever given to charity or volunteered? What did you do, and how did it feel?
Some say helping the poor should be the government's job, not individuals'. Do you agree — why?
Is it better to give help openly (to inspire others) or anonymously? Why?

a.title: International Literacy Day
text: September 8 is International Literacy Day. It was started by UNESCO, a part of the United Nations.
To be literate means you can read and write. Reading and writing help people learn, work, and understand the world.
Today, most children go to school. But some people never learn to read. Around the world, hundreds of millions of adults still cannot read well.
Many of them are women and girls. In some places, girls do not get the same chance to go to school as boys.
On this day, schools and groups talk about why reading matters. They also help people who want to learn to read.
Reading opens doors. When you can read, you can learn almost anything.

q.q: What is this text mainly about?
opts: A day about reading and writing, and why they matter
q.why: 全文介紹國際識字日，以及閱讀與書寫為什麼重要。

q.q: Who started International Literacy Day?
opts: UNESCO, part of the United Nations
q.why: 第一段：It was started by UNESCO, a part of the United Nations。

q.q: According to the text, who often cannot read?
q.why: 第四段：Many of them are women and girls。

q.q: “Literate” means a person who ___.
q.why: literate = 識字的，也就是會讀會寫。

q.q: Why does the text say “Reading opens doors”?
opts: Because reading lets you learn almost anything
Because doors are made of paper
q.why: 末段說會閱讀就能學幾乎任何事，「開啟大門」比喻帶來許多機會。

b.title: Why Reading Still Matters
text: Each year on 8 September, the world marks International Literacy Day, an event created by UNESCO in 1966 to remind us how powerful reading and writing can be.

Literacy is more than a school skill. A person who can read can follow health advice, understand a job contract, use a phone safely, and take part in public life. Without it, everyday tasks become far harder.

Progress has been real. The global literacy rate has risen above 86 percent, and most children now start school. Yet the United Nations estimates that around 760 million adults still cannot read a simple sentence, and about two-thirds of them are women.
The gap is widest in poorer regions, where children may leave school early to work, and where girls in particular are often kept at home. Wars and natural disasters can also close schools for years.
Technology brings both hope and worry. Phones and apps can teach reading to people far from any school, but they can also spread false information that readers must learn to judge carefully.
The message of the day is simple: reading is a right, not a luxury, and a society that reads is a fairer and freer one.

q.q: Which sentence best states the main idea?
opts: Everyone in the world can now read.
Literacy matters deeply, and although the world has improved, millions still cannot read.
q.why: 全文兩大重點：閱讀非常重要；雖有進步，仍有數億人不識字。

q.q: How many adults still cannot read a simple sentence?
q.why: 第三段：the United Nations estimates that around 760 million adults still cannot read a simple sentence。

q.q: Where is the literacy gap widest?
opts: In poorer regions, where children leave school early
q.why: 第四段：The gap is widest in poorer regions…children may leave school early to work。

q.q: In the last paragraph, calling reading “a right, not a luxury” means it should be ___.
opts: available to everyone, not a treat for a few
q.why: a right, not a luxury = 是「權利」而非「奢侈品」，即人人都應享有，而非少數人的享受。

q.q: Why does the writer say technology brings “both hope and worry”?
opts: It can teach reading, but also spread false information
q.why: 第五段：手機與 App 能教人閱讀（hope），但也會散播假訊息，需要讀者謹慎判斷（worry）。

c.title: The Quiet Power of a Sentence
text: On 8 September the world observes International Literacy Day, an occasion that can seem, at first glance, almost quaint. In an era of instant translation and talking machines, why celebrate something as basic as reading a sentence?

The answer is that literacy remains the hinge on which almost everything else turns. To read is to gain access — to medicine, to law, to work, and to the right to question those in power. The United Nations estimates that some 760 million adults still lack that access, and that women make up nearly two-thirds of them, a statistic that quietly shapes the fate of whole families.

The story is neither simple decline nor easy triumph. Global literacy has climbed past 86 percent, a remarkable achievement in a single century. But averages conceal sharp divides: between rich regions and poor, between boys who stay in school and girls who are called home, between peacetime classrooms and those emptied by war.

Technology complicates the picture further. The same phone that can teach a child to read in a village without a school can also flood that child with claims she has no easy way to test. Literacy, in other words, is no longer only about decoding words; it is increasingly about weighing them.

That is why the day endures. It insists that the ability to read — and to read critically — is not a private convenience but a public good, and that a society is only as free as its least literate member.

q.q: Which best captures the writer's overall point?
opts: Literacy is old-fashioned and no longer needed.
Reading remains essential — and today also means judging information critically.
Machines can now read for everyone.
q.why: 作者主張識字仍是關鍵，且在資訊時代更需要「批判性地閱讀」（weighing words）。

q.q: In paragraph 1, “quaint” suggests the day seems ___.
q.why: quaint = 古雅、有點過時可愛的。作者說乍看之下，慶祝「讀一句話」好像有點過時——再加以反駁。

q.q: What does the writer mean by literacy being “the hinge on which almost everything else turns”?
opts: Reading is a small, unimportant detail
Reading is the key that gives access to almost everything else
q.why: hinge（樞紐）比喻識字是取得醫療、法律、工作與質疑權力等一切的「關鍵」。

q.q: What is the purpose of paragraph 3 (“neither simple decline nor easy triumph”)?
opts: To prove literacy is falling everywhere
To show a mixed picture: real progress, but sharp remaining divides
q.why: 第三段呈現「有進步、但差距仍深」的複雜面貌，avoid 一面倒的悲觀或樂觀。

q.q: The final sentence (“only as free as its least literate member”) is meant to ___.
opts: make a strong moral point about fairness and freedom
q.why: 結尾以「一個社會的自由，取決於其中識字能力最弱的人」作道德呼籲，強調公平與自由。

discuss: Reading is called “a right, not a luxury.” Do you agree? Why?
Some people read fewer books now and watch more videos. Does it matter — why or why not?
With so much information online, how can students learn to tell what is true from what is false?

topic: USA Win a Fifth Straight Basketball World Cup
zh: 美國女籃世界盃五連霸
src: NBC · The New York Times · FIBA

a.title: The USA Win the Basketball World Cup
text: The United States women's basketball team won the World Cup on Sunday, September 13. The final game was in Berlin, Germany.
The USA played against France. The USA won 97 to 79. It was a big win.
This is the fifth time in a row that the USA has won the World Cup. The team is very strong.
France played well at the start. At half-time, France was winning 45 to 43.
But in the third quarter, the USA played much better and took the lead. After that, France could not catch up.
Breanna Stewart was the best player for the USA. She scored 22 points. Fans all around the world watched the final.

q.q: What is this text mainly about?
opts: The USA winning the Basketball World Cup
q.why: 全文都在講美國女籃在世界盃奪冠：比分、連霸、怎麼贏的。

q.q: What was the final score?
q.why: 第二段：the USA won 97 to 79。

q.q: How many times in a row has the USA won the World Cup?
q.why: 第三段：the fifth time in a row（連續第五次）。

q.q: In the text, “in a row” means ___.
opts: one after another, with no breaks
q.why: in a row = 連續、接連不斷。fifth time in a row 就是「連續第五次」。

q.q: Why could France not win?
opts: They did not come to the game
The USA played much better in the third quarter
q.why: 第四、五段：法國上半場領先，但第三節美國表現好很多、超前，之後法國追不上。

b.title: USA Beat France for a Fifth Consecutive Title
text: The United States won the 2026 Women's Basketball World Cup on Sunday, 13 September, beating France 97–79 in the final in Berlin, Germany.
It was a repeat of the Paris 2024 Olympic final, and once again the Americans came out on top. The victory gave the USA their fifth World Cup title in a row, and their twelfth in total.
France, however, did not make it easy. Led by young centre Dominique Malonga, who scored 21 points, and Gabby Williams, who added 20, France led 45–43 at half-time.

The turning point came in the third quarter. The USA outscored France 30–12 in those ten minutes, turning a narrow deficit into a comfortable lead. Breanna Stewart top-scored for the champions with 22 points, 10 rebounds and 4 assists, while Jackie Young added 18.
The result extended an extraordinary run: the USA have now won 36 World Cup games in a row, a streak that goes back to the semi-finals of the 2006 tournament.
Germany, the host nation, drew large and enthusiastic crowds throughout the tournament, a sign of how quickly women's basketball is growing around the world.

q.q: Which sentence best states the main idea?
opts: The USA beat France to win a fifth straight World Cup title.
Dominique Malonga is the best player in the world.
Basketball is more popular than soccer.
q.why: 首段與全文重點都是：美國擊敗法國、拿下連續第五冠。其他都是細節或文中沒有的比較。

q.q: What happened in the third quarter?
opts: France scored more and pulled ahead.
The USA outscored France 30–12 and took control.
q.why: 第四段：the USA outscored France 30–12，把小幅落後翻轉成穩定領先。

q.q: In paragraph 4, “deficit” is closest in meaning to ___.
opts: the amount by which a team is behind
q.why: deficit 指「落後的分差」。整句說美國把 narrow deficit（小幅落後）變成 comfortable lead（穩定領先）。

q.q: What does the 36-game winning streak suggest about the USA team?
opts: They have been dominant for a very long time.
q.why: 連勝 36 場、自 2006 年起未曾在世界盃輸球，代表他們長期稱霸。

q.q: How was this final connected to Paris 2024?
opts: It was a repeat of the Paris 2024 Olympic final.
Both teams were new to the final.
q.why: 第二段：It was a repeat of the Paris 2024 Olympic final —— 同樣是美國對法國。

c.title: A Dynasty Rolls On — and a Rival Rises
text: There are dynasties, and then there is the United States women's basketball team. By defeating France 97–79 in Berlin on Sunday, the Americans claimed a fifth consecutive World Cup title and extended a winning run that now stands at 36 games, unbroken since 2006. In a sport increasingly shaped by global competition, such sustained dominance is almost an anomaly.

Yet the final scoreline flattered the winners. For a half, France not only competed but led, 45–43, powered by the twenty-one points of Dominique Malonga, a centre still in the early years of a career many believe will reshape the international game. It was only in the third quarter — that familiar American crucible — that the match turned, the champions outscoring their opponents 30–12 and, within ten minutes, converting a deficit into a procession.

Breanna Stewart, with 22 points and 10 rebounds, was once again the fulcrum of the American effort. But the more telling story may belong to the losers. As a repeat of the Paris 2024 Olympic final, this was a second successive gold-medal meeting between the two nations — evidence, perhaps, that the gap at the very top is narrowing, even if it has not yet closed.

For Germany, the host, the tournament was a success in its own right, drawing large crowds to venues across the country. Whether any team can finally end the American streak is a question that will now wait, as these tournaments do, for another four years.

q.q: Which best captures the writer's overall point?
opts: France deserved to win the final.
The USA's long dominance continues, but France's rise hints the gap is narrowing.
Germany should not have hosted the tournament.
q.why: 標題 A Dynasty Rolls On — and a Rival Rises 已點出雙主軸：美國霸業延續（第1段），法國崛起、差距縮小（第3段）。

q.q: In paragraph 2, “the scoreline flattered the winners” means the final score ___.
opts: made the USA look better than the game really was
was too low for the USA
q.why: flatter 指「使…顯得比實際更好」。作者接著說法國上半場其實領先，所以 97–79 這個差距讓美國看起來比實際過程更輕鬆。

q.q: Why does the writer say the more telling story “may belong to the losers”?
opts: France played badly and should be ashamed.
France's strong showing may signal that the top gap is closing.
France will never reach a final again.
The USA played the losers' bracket.
q.why: 第3段：連兩屆金牌戰都是美法對決、法國上半場領先，暗示頂尖差距正在縮小——重點反而在輸家身上。

q.q: How does the writer treat the USA's dominance?
opts: With admiration, while noting it may not last forever
As proof the sport is boring
q.why: 作者稱其為 dynasty、almost an anomaly（讚賞其罕見），但結尾又留下「差距縮小、能否終結連勝」的伏筆，並非一面倒吹捧。

q.q: What is the role of “Yet” at the start of paragraph 2?
opts: To add more praise for the USA
To signal a contrast: the game was closer than the score suggests
q.why: Yet 為轉折。第1段講美國壓倒性紀錄，第2段用 Yet 轉向「比分其實美化了過程，法國一度領先」。

discuss: Is it good for a sport when one team wins for so long? Why or why not?
What makes a great team — talent, teamwork, or something else? Give an example.
Women's sports are getting more attention around the world. How could we support them in Taiwan?

src: Taiwan News · Taipei Times · The New York Times

a.title: The Mid-Autumn Festival
text: The Mid-Autumn Festival is a special holiday in Taiwan and many parts of Asia. In 2026, it falls on Friday, September 25.
The festival happens in autumn, when the moon is big, round, and bright. People say the moon is most beautiful on this night.
Families come together to eat, talk, and look at the moon. A round moon is a symbol of a happy, whole family.
People eat mooncakes. A mooncake is a small round cake with sweet or salty filling inside.
In Taiwan, many families also have a barbecue outside. They cook meat and vegetables with friends and neighbors.
Children play with bright lanterns. It is a warm and happy night for everyone.

q.q: What is this text mainly about?
opts: The Mid-Autumn Festival and how people celebrate it
q.why: 全文都在介紹中秋節：時間、月亮、團圓、月餅、烤肉、燈籠。

q.q: When is the festival in 2026?
q.why: 第一段：In 2026, it falls on Friday, September 25。

q.q: What is a mooncake?
opts: A small round cake with filling inside
q.why: 第四段：a mooncake is a small round cake with sweet or salty filling inside。

q.q: In the text, “symbol” means ___.
opts: something that stands for an idea
q.why: symbol = 象徵。圓月象徵「圓滿、團圓的家庭」。

q.q: Why is the round moon important on this night?
opts: It is the only night with a moon
Its round shape stands for a happy, whole family
q.why: 第三段：a round moon is a symbol of a happy, whole family——圓月象徵團圓。

b.title: One Bright Moon, Many Traditions
text: Every autumn, millions of people across Asia look up at the same full moon to celebrate the Mid-Autumn Festival. In 2026 it falls on 25 September — the fifteenth day of the eighth month in the lunar calendar.
The festival is a time for family reunion. The round shape of the moon stands for wholeness and togetherness, and relatives often travel long distances to share a meal at home.

Food is central to the celebration. The most famous treat is the mooncake, a dense pastry filled with lotus-seed paste, red bean, or salted egg yolk. In recent years, bakeries have created modern flavours such as chocolate, ice cream, and even matcha.

Different places keep different customs. In Taiwan, outdoor barbecues have become hugely popular since the 1980s, and the smell of grilled food fills neighbourhoods on festival night. In Vietnam and elsewhere, children parade with colourful lanterns.

Behind the festival lies an old legend about Chang'e, the Moon Goddess, who is said to have flown to the moon and to live there still. Many parents tell her story to their children while sharing tea and mooncakes.
Whatever the custom, the message is the same: a moment to slow down, look up at the sky, and be with the people we love.

q.q: Which sentence best states the main idea?
opts: Across Asia, people celebrate the Mid-Autumn Festival with shared traditions of family, food, and the moon.
The moon is bigger in autumn.
q.why: 全文圍繞「同一輪明月下、各地以團圓、飲食與賞月來慶祝中秋」。

q.q: According to the text, the festival date is based on ___.
opts: the lunar calendar — the 15th day of the 8th month
q.why: 第一段：the fifteenth day of the eighth month in the lunar calendar。

q.q: What does the text say about barbecues in Taiwan?
opts: They are banned on festival night
They have been popular since the 1980s
q.why: 第四段：outdoor barbecues have become hugely popular since the 1980s。

q.q: In paragraph 2, “reunion” is closest in meaning to ___.
q.why: reunion = 團圓、重聚。家人從遠方回家團聚。

q.q: What does the paragraph about new mooncake flavours suggest?
opts: Traditions can change and stay alive at the same time
Old mooncakes are no longer sold
q.why: 傳統月餅出現巧克力、冰淇淋、抹茶等新口味，說明傳統會隨時代改變、卻依然延續。

c.title: The Moon That Binds
text: Few celebrations capture a culture's imagination as completely as the Mid-Autumn Festival, observed this year on 25 September. For a single night, a scattered population turns its collective gaze upward, drawn together not by a flag or an anthem but by the oldest of shared symbols: a full, luminous moon.

At its heart the festival is about reunion. The perfect circle overhead has long been read as a metaphor for the family made whole, and even in an age of video calls, the pull to return home in person remains remarkably strong. Highways fill; kitchens crowd; the elderly wait by the door.

Its foods and rituals, however, are anything but static. The mooncake — once a dense, formal gift of lotus paste and salted yolk — has been reinvented by bakeries competing to launch ever more inventive flavours, from champagne truffle to salted-caramel custard. In Taiwan, the tradition of the outdoor barbecue, barely forty years old, now rivals the mooncake itself — a reminder that “ancient” customs are often surprisingly modern.

Underneath runs the myth of Chang'e, the woman who swallowed an elixir of immortality and drifted, alone, to the moon. It is a story of sacrifice and separation as much as of magic — a quiet counterweight to the festival's warmth, and perhaps part of why the round moon moves us so.
That, in the end, may be the festival's genius: it holds joy and longing in the same glance, and asks only that we look up together.

q.q: Which best captures the writer's overall point?
opts: Mooncakes taste better than they used to.
The festival endures because it unites people and holds both joy and longing together.
Video calls have replaced family reunions.
q.why: 全文說中秋把離散的人凝聚，並在同一眼神裡容納喜悅與思念（末段），這才是它歷久不衰的原因。

q.q: In paragraph 3, “anything but static” means the foods and rituals are ___.
opts: far from unchanging — they keep evolving
q.why: static = 一成不變；anything but static = 「絕非一成不變」，即不斷改變。

q.q: Why does the writer call the Taiwanese barbecue a reminder that “‘ancient’ customs are often surprisingly modern”?
opts: Because barbecues are older than mooncakes
Because a beloved festival tradition is in fact only about forty years old
q.why: 烤肉這個「看似傳統」的中秋習俗其實才約四十年歷史，說明許多所謂古老習俗其實很新。

q.q: How does the writer treat the legend of Chang'e?
opts: As a darker note of sacrifice that balances the festival's warmth
q.why: 第四段把嫦娥視為犧牲與別離的故事，是節慶溫暖的「抗衡」（counterweight），為歡樂添上一層惆悵。

q.q: What is the role of the word “However” in paragraph 3?
opts: To signal a contrast — from reunion to how much the customs change
q.why: 第二段談團圓的恆常，第三段用 however 轉向「飲食與習俗其實不斷改變」，形成對比。
